title: Taiwan Detects 28 PLA Aircraft Sorties, 24 Crossing Median Line — Highest Crossing Count Since Sept 7 Window High
detail: Taiwan's Ministry of National Defense detected 28 PLA aircraft sorties, 7 PLAN vessels and 2 official ships operating around Taiwan in the 24 hours to 6 a.m. (UTC+8) September 18, 2026; 24 of the 28 sorties crossed the Taiwan Strait median line, entering the northern, central, southwestern and eastern ADIZ sectors. Taiwan's armed forces responded with CAP aircraft, navy ships and coastal missile systems. The 24 median-line crossings are the most recorded in a single window since the Sept 7 surge (29 sorties, 17 crossing), and mark the fifth consecutive day of rising PLA activity (4 on Sept 14, 8 on Sept 15, 15 on Sept 16, 19 on Sept 17), coinciding with the final day of Taiwan's own Jioupeng Base precision-strike live-fire drill and President Lai's on-site inspection.

title: Lai Inspects Final Day of Jioupeng Drill as Chinese Recon Drone Shadows Exercise Off Taitung
detail: President William Lai inspected the final day of the three-day joint precision-strike live-fire drill at Jioupeng Base in Pingtung County on September 18, 2026, which for the first time incorporated multiple types of attack drones — including ALTIUS-600M loitering munitions and Switchblade drones — into joint combat exercises alongside Tien Kung III surface-to-air missiles, Hsiung Feng III anti-ship missiles and US-made HIMARS launchers striking designated targets. Taiwan's Ministry of National Defense said a Chinese military drone flew from Taiwan's southwestern airspace to waters off Taitung County between 12:05 a.m. and 6 a.m. that morning to monitor the exercise; because the timing coincided with Lai's inspection, the military closely tracked the drone and deployed aircraft, naval vessels and land-based missile systems in response. Military sources said the navy's Chien Lung-class submarines would not fire torpedoes during this drill as earlier reported, with a separate torpedo exercise expected at a later date.

title: Premier Cho Launches Taiwan-Matsu No. 4 Subsea Cable as Communications-Resilience Backstop
detail: Premier Cho Jung-tai inaugurated the Taiwan-Matsu Subsea Cable No. 4 in Lienchiang County on September 18, 2026, calling it part of the government's 'preemptive preparations' to bolster communications resilience for the outlying Matsu Islands. The NT$1.4 billion (~US$44 million) cable, built by Dong Fang Offshore, spans 294 kilometers connecting New Taipei's Bali District with Dongyin, Nangan and Juguang townships in Lienchiang County, lifting total transmission capacity to about 1.9 terabits per second and providing backup capacity should other undersea links be damaged. The launch follows repeated disruptions to Matsu's connectivity since February 2023, including shipping-related cable cuts, some attributed to Chinese vessels, that left the islands without stable internet service for weeks at a time. Cho said future resilience plans would also draw on microwave links and low-orbit satellites.

title: MAC Deputy Minister Shen Yu-chung: US Remains Committed to First Island Chain Deterrence
detail: Mainland Affairs Council Deputy Minister Shen Yu-chung said on September 18, 2026 that the United States remains committed to maintaining deterrence along the first island chain, and that Taipei has received messages indicating this remains a US policy priority. Speaking at a National Chengchi University seminar on China's trajectory since the CCP's 20th National Congress, Shen was responding to warnings from former National Security Council Secretary-General Su Chi about rising Taiwan Strait risk and declining US security commitment. Shen also clarified Foreign Minister Lin Chia-lung's earlier remark about Taiwan and the US 'jointly managing China,' saying 'jointly managing China means jointly managing risks — it does not mean managing mainland China,' and said Taiwan would watch closely whether President Trump reiterates an unchanged Taiwan policy during his September 24 meeting with Xi Jinping.
